channel.title: CrooHQ Blog
channel.description: Operator notes from CrooHQ founder Jordan Andrian on restaurant scheduling, time punches, labor, and running a calmer shift.

item.title: Seven Questions Multi-Unit Owners Ask Me, and My Straight Answers
item.description: Seven questions multi-unit fast-casual owners ask about staffing, labor, and being in more than one place, answered the way I'd answer them over coffee.

item.title: Geofenced Clock-In vs. a PIN Pad: How to Choose for Your Restaurant
item.description: Should crews punch in from their phones inside a geofence or on a PIN pad at the store? Here's an operator's way to compare them.

item.title: How to Onboard a New Crew Member in Their First Three Shifts
item.description: A new hire decides whether to stay in the first few shifts. Here's a shift-by-shift plan for fast-casual crews, with a hypothetical example.

item.title: A Missed Punch Policy Template for Restaurant Crews
item.description: Forgotten punches are normal. A written missed punch policy keeps them from turning into payroll arguments. Copy this template and adjust it for your stores.

item.title: Shift Swap Rules That Don't Blow Up Your Overtime
item.description: Shift swaps feel like a favor to your crew until one pushes someone past 40 hours. Here are the swap rules I'd put in writing for a fast-casual crew.

item.title: Opening and Closing Checklists Your Crew Will Actually Finish
item.description: Paper checklists get ignored. Here's how fast-casual operators keep opening and closing tasks done — and visible across every location.

item.title: Your Closer Just Quit by Text at 10:02 PM. Now What?
item.description: A closer quits by text after closing. An operator's playbook for covering the shift without burning your best people — and what Theo does when you ask him.

item.title: How to Run Three Stores Without Living in Your Car
item.description: Multi-unit fast-casual owners can't be in every store. Here's how to keep schedules, punches, and checklists honest when you're across town.

item.title: Shift Handoff Notes: What the Closing Manager Must Pass On
item.description: A closing manager's handoff should take two minutes and save the opener an hour. Here's the note format that actually gets read.

item.title: Theo Isn't a Chatbot. He's the Manager's Shift Partner.
item.description: Theo is CrooHQ's voice AI agent inside the app. Here's what he can do on a real shift — coverage, punches, sales projections — and what he won't pretend to do.

item.title: Buddy Punching: How to Spot It and Stop It Without Treating Your Crew Like Suspects
item.description: Buddy punching quietly inflates labor in restaurants. An operator's guide to spotting the patterns and shutting it down without souring your crew.

item.title: When the Punches Don't Match the Paycheck
item.description: Monday punch cleanup eating your morning? An operator's guide to why time punches and schedules drift apart, and how to catch it before payroll.

item.title: Your Schedule Shouldn't Live in a Group Text
item.description: Shift swaps lost in the group chat leave you short on Saturday. An operator's take on keeping one schedule everyone trusts, swaps and pickups included.
